directorExistingCase.title: Hazards, difficulty, exploration and pressure
directorExistingCase.question: Retain the three clue types and defined stakes while reconciling the manual DC bands with current Core check degrees and actual item/class limits. Source ten-minute turns, four pressure tracks, d6/d8/d10 thresholds, automatic six trigger and rest durations route to the existing 26-case expedition conference. Supply actual authored hazard effects, detection/disarm/trigger/recovery timing and finite failure outcomes in that authority; a generic scaled injury is not a completed hazard. No default permanent loss or invented tier cosmology.

directorBlocks.text: Falling, environmental hazards, and other single-check situations. Default to the simplest fair resolution: an appropriate save or check, with damage or a condition scaled to the fictional severity, rather than inventing bespoke sub-systems for every environmental hazard. Save your bespoke-mechanic effort for hazards that recur often enough to be worth teaching the table (a tier's signature threat), not one-off flavor.

The Player Rulebook divides expedition days into morning, afternoon, and evening periods. Inside a hazardous floor, the Director needs a smaller unit. Use the exploration turn: approximately ten minutes of careful movement, searching, treatment, harvesting, repair, or focused investigation. Six exploration turns equal one hour of the Opening. Do not force this procedure during free conversation or a dramatic scene; use it when time, noise, supply, or exposure matters.
1. Declare. The acting team states its objective and approach. “Search the western wall for a mechanical seam” is actionable; “I investigate everything” is not.
2. Assign time. Most focused actions take one turn. Complex treatment, harvesting, ritual work, or moving through severe terrain may take two or more.
3. Resolve. Make only the checks that uncertainty requires. A correct tool, specific description, or prior discovery may remove the need for a roll.
4. Advance pressure. Mark elapsed time and update any relevant tracks.
5. Reveal consequence. Give the result, including what the character learns about the risk. Failure should change the situation, not merely produce “nothing happens.”

rows: Fights, forced doors, loud spells, failed stealth, metalwork
Patrol interest / active hunt / major encounter or route closure
Food, light, medicine, ammunition, filters, protective salves
Minor shortage / team penalty or hard choice / forced retreat or dangerous substitution
Heat, spores, radiance, resonance, cold, hush, corruption
Discomfort / condition or gear damage / severe injury, mutation, or floor-specific crisis
Taking relics, breaking wards, repeated Gate contact, harming floor citizens
Omen / targeted response / elite response, faction intervention, or Guardian echo

directorBlocks.text: Tracks are Director instruments, not universal player statistics. Tell players what their characters can perceive: the air is becoming harder to breathe, tracks show a patrol changing course, the lantern oil is below half. You may show the numerical track if your table prefers explicit resource play, but the fiction must remain primary.

When a track rises and the next consequence is uncertain, roll a pressure die. Use d6 for early tiers, d8 for middle tiers, and d10 for Tiers 7–10. A result at or below the current track triggers a complication. The die does not decide whether the world reacts; it decides whether the reaction arrives now. A track at 6 triggers automatically and then falls by 2 after the consequence resolves, unless the situation clearly continues to worsen.

Do not hide required progress behind one check. If the Expedition must find the Gate key to continue, place at least three independent leads to it. Checks determine speed, cost, completeness, or whether a complication occurs. They should not determine whether the campaign simply stops. Optional treasure, shortcuts, and deeper lore may remain missable.

A short or long rest is never free merely because the rules allow it. The party must have time and a plausible location. A long rest advances the Opening by eight hours, consumes supplies, and gives rivals and factions time to move. In an exposed location, the party may need to spend turns concealing the camp, setting watches, or bargaining for shelter. Denying every rest is punitive; granting every rest without consequence erases the expedition game.

rows: Use Pressure to Make Choices, Not to Punish

Raise pressure when the Expedition takes actions that logically create it. Do not add Noise because the party succeeded too easily or increase Exposure because you want to force a fight. Pressure is credible only when players can understand what caused it and choose differently next time.

directorBlocks.text: A trap is a decision waiting to happen, not a hidden packet of damage. The best hazards announce enough of themselves that careful players can choose an approach, then remain dangerous because acting under pressure is difficult. Use traps to reveal the dungeon’s priorities: what it protects, what behavior it rewards, and what kind of expedition it was built to attract.

rows: The clue is clear and the danger is modest
Lost time, noise, or minor resource cost
A trained adventurer has a fair chance
A meaningful complication or small injury
The task is dangerous under expedition conditions
Damage, condition, broken gear, route loss, or pressure increase
Specialized skill, tools, or preparation are expected
Severe cost or a major change in the scene

Use sparingly and always provide ways to reduce the DC or bypass the roll

directorBlocks.text: Before a serious trap, provide three types of clue whenever possible: environmental evidence, behavioral evidence, and structural evidence. Scorch marks are environmental. A corpse gripping an unburned metal rod is behavioral. Repeating runes around one tile are structural. A player may notice one clue automatically because of their stated approach; checks reveal additional detail or reduce the cost of acting.

A failed disarm should usually trigger one of four results: the hazard activates but leaves a path, the character avoids the worst effect by sacrificing gear or position, the party succeeds but raises Noise or Attention, or the mechanism changes and demands a different solution. Reserve total route denial for optional areas or for situations with a clearly signposted alternate route.

Use lasting injuries only when the table agreed to them, the fiction clearly supports them, and the injury creates play rather than simply removing competence. Good injuries have a treatment path, a temporary adaptation, and a story consequence. A cracked arm brace that requires Support attention and changes how a Warrior fights is playable. “You permanently lose your best ability” is usually not.

operational.targets: One point you perceive within 30 feet and line of effect, on your current plane.
operational.duration: Instantaneous information about the following 24 hours; no continuing buff or concentration.
operational.resolution: No roll. The Director gives an accurate 24-hour forecast for the local outdoor region within 1 mile horizontally of that point on the same plane. Describe meaningful local variations when the terrain makes the region's weather differ. An indoor or underground point refers to the outdoor local weather above/around that same geographical location rather than the room's climate.
operational.effect: Report relevant temperature bands/trends, precipitation type and approximate timing, wind direction/strength, weather-caused visibility and significant storm or environmental-weather hazards. The report is intelligible to the caster and accurate for the current natural processes and already-existing magical weather expected to continue; record the forecast as the current weather expectation. A weatherless environment reports that fact. It supplies useful specific conditions rather than a vague warning that weather might change.
operational.scaling: None. No automatic increase in targets, range, duration or information.
operational.limitations: A genuinely new later cause, such as a voluntary weather-changing spell, new supernatural event or catastrophe, can change actual conditions after the forecast without having been predicted. The Director must identify an actual intervening cause in the game record, not silently invalidate the forecast by rerolling unchanged weather; this need not reveal that cause to the caster. The spell does not control weather, grant exposure protection, reveal encounters/loot, complete travel, recover resources or predict unrelated events. Information about a specifically protected subject remains limited by that actual protection; ordinary ambient weather is not automatically protected by a creature standing in it. Actual class access and repertoire, audible V/free-hand S components, casting sequence, Refrain/Dissonance, class hooks and interruption follow SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md. Base RP is 0 but repeated cantrips still follow their actual strain rules. No automatic upcast or unstated scaling. Source-specific protections apply only to their actual scope. Protection from Scrying prevents new Divination/Scrying information about its protected subject, including beneficial inspection, but grants no blanket immunity to damage, buffs or other noninformational mechanics merely because of their school; it does not erase already-known facts or ordinary records.

NEW: finite1-mile local outdoor region, explicit indoor reference, forecast fields and current-processes/future-agency boundary. This is a tabletop forecast record, not a claim a weather simulation is implemented.

### Core Burning — `core.burning`

At end of the affected creature's regular turn its generic record offers 1d4 fire damage to unified family arbitration, unless its source specifies another magnitude. Only the winning stack group deals damage. Damage immunity does not by itself remove Burning.

**Ending:** Self or adjacent helper may spend one Action to end all active ordinary-extinguishable attached fires on this creature. Full immersion of all burning portions does the same. Explicit protected-source exceptions survive. At each regular target turn end, after due ticks are consumed, each surviving active ongoing-fire record with future damage remaining makes its own binary DEX save against its own source DC or 10. Success ends only that record. An indefinite generic fire counts as having future damage; a finite record with its final tick consumed expires without another save.

**Stacking:** Independent records enter unified ongoing-fire family arbitration. One Action/full immersion clears all ordinary-extinguishable records; DEX saves operate per surviving eligible record, not one selected-source save for all fires.
**Immunity:** Fire immunity prevents the damage but does not automatically end Burning unless the source or immunity says so. An effect explicitly immune to Burning blocks application.

Reuse current rest and expedition clocks; do not create free resets or double-charge the same exposure. Separate ordinary environmental hazards from each source-specific supernatural effect.

questions.title: Breathing and suffocation
questions.question: Locate or author the baseline for holding breath, loss of breathable air, interrupted rescue and suffocation, with finite timing, checks, damage/state changes and recovery. Preserve actual anatomy and water-breathing permissions; neither damage resistance nor generic immunity to a condition supplies breathable air.

questions.title: Heat and cold exposure
questions.question: Define the referenced extreme-heat/cold thresholds, exposure interval, exact saves and outcomes, shelter/equipment eligibility and recovery. Core brew Stoneback Stout says to ignore the first level of cold-weather exposure for four hours. Preserve that complete consumable source; do not assume that a completed recipe review approved this separate brew or defined an exposure scale.

questions.title: Open flames and ongoing fire
questions.question: Separate entering/remaining in an actual fire from an effect that explicitly applies Burning. Bind ignition, damage frequency, extinguishing, full immersion, immunity, suppression and multiple records to the reviewed ongoing-fire family; do not apply a second generic tick for one event.

questions.title: Smoke, gases and visibility
questions.question: Specify actual visibility, inhalation and breathable-air consequences separately. Define geometry, ventilation, dissipating and moving volumes where needed; obey actual sight/targeting rules and source-specific gas counters. A dispersed ordinary smoke cube does not create continuing air or end a magical cloud.

questions.title: Water, currents and rescue
questions.question: Connect movement, swimming, carrying, currents, submersion and rescue to the breathing baseline. Keep water breathing distinct from swim speed, depth/temperature protection and freedom of movement. Ending a form or spell restores actual anatomy at the current location without free relocation.

questions.title: Weather and forecasts
questions.question: Give Directors a usable record of actual temperature, precipitation, wind and visibility. Preserve Detect Weather accuracy and its actual later-cause exception; class weather moderation and winter invocations retain their bounded scope. Do not add planar, seasonal or decennial setting interpretation.

questions.title: Environmental poison
questions.question: Define exposure routes, dose identity, timing, save/outcome, persistence and countermeasures for each actual hazard. Keep poison damage, Poisoned and suffocation independent; route reviewed poisoncrafting delivery and cure rules without reopening completed recipe effects or granting blanket immunity.

questions.title: Disease and contagion
questions.question: Identify actual supported disease sources and give each transmission route, onset, checks, progression, treatment and ending. Bind creature disease features to the pending bestiary source conference; do not infer a universal disease from a flavor label or turn one cure into future immunity.

questions.title: Corrosive and unstable terrain
questions.question: Define finite procedures for actual acids, unstable ground, entrapment and similar supported hazards. Preserve object versus creature targeting, damage-type scope, structural HP and existing gear identity. Director severity advice alone does not specify complete damage or a permanent equipment-loss rule.

questions.title: Traps and finite failure
questions.question: Use the Director manual clue/disarm guidance and reviewed device/recipe procedures. Supply concrete detection, interaction, trigger, target geometry, outcome, reset and disarm records; settle failure costs before the roll and preserve alternate routes. Do not convert suggested setbacks into automatic permanent losses.

questions.title: Falls and forced movement
questions.question: Use the already-reviewed falling/geometry/movement procedure for actual height, rescue opportunities, flight loss and landing. Establish only missing environmental trigger interfaces; do not recreate or contradict the existing fall calculation or invent collision damage from forced movement alone.

questions.title: Actual protection and scope
questions.question: Map each actual ancestry/class/spell/item protection to the precise hazard predicate it changes. Distinguish advantage, resistance, ignored ordinary penalties, immunity and shelter; preserve forms, worn/functional/melded equipment and shared modifier families. Pending ordinary spells remain pending.

questions.question: Create complete cases for ongoing exposure interrupted by rest, shelter, rescue, transformation, treatment and a Watch boundary.
